headline: Banjo Loans sees stable SME arrears despite tough economic conditions, flagging 'alert but not alarmed' posture
reasoning: Guy Callaghan notes that arrears across Banjo Loans' SME borrower base have remained consistent over the past three years despite a difficult economic environment post-COVID. He attributes this stability to business owners being highly attuned to their cash flows and meeting their financial commitments diligently. The major banks have been monitoring SME stress closely and have been in dialogue with Banjo, but Callaghan says the outcome has been pleasing. Post-budget, he characterises activity as 'business as usual,' noting the CGT changes don't materially affect Banjo's lending focus (cash flow lending rather than business sale finance), and that the instant asset write-off extension was largely already expected by the market.
quote: Look. And that's something we've been really, um, we've been really monitoring quite, um, diligently. I mean, we always do. But, you know, as I said, some of the majors are concerned, so, so that that sort of chatting to us, but we're, we're monitoring it really diligently and probably our, our saying at the moment is we're, we're alert, but we're not alarmed. And pleasingly, we are just seeing business as usual with arrears. And I think what that means is, you know, we had Covid a while back and then we have had a really tough economy and business owners are really attuned to it, and they actually know their cash flow really well. And as a consequence, they're really attuned to the cash commitments that they've got and being really diligent about keeping them up there.
episode_title: A new era for SME finance
